fields.statement: With rhiza.daemon.maxRuns=auto each poll's machine-wide cap is the runs running plus one when every pre-start check (load and memory machine hold, tmp-low hold, the home project's disk-low check) has room, and the runs running when any holds, so each further start waits for the next poll's fresh readings
fields.wording: (planner ruling, derived from the intent and the daemon's pre-start checks; would have escalated)

fields.statement: auto is a value of rhiza.daemon.maxRuns only: the default stays 2, a number still pins the cap, and rhiza.project.maxRuns and the daemon's --max-runs flag stay whole numbers
fields.wording: (planner ruling, derived from the intent's 'a number still pins the limit'; would have escalated)

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'MaxRuns' and go test -trimpath ./internal/tui/daemonapp/...: a test sets rhiza.daemon.maxRuns to auto and reads auto back with daemonConf marked auto, a test sets 3 and gets a pinned cap of 3, and the daemon app accepts auto in its run-limit field; (failure case) 0, -1 and autox are refused for rhiza.daemon.maxRuns with an error naming 'a whole number of at least 1 or auto', and auto is refused for rhiza.project.maxRuns
fields.must_not: Change the default of 2, the --max-runs flag's whole-number type, or rhiza.project.maxRuns; change how the poll starts runs (leaf maxruns-auto-poll)
fields.statement: rhiza.daemon.maxRuns accepts auto beside a whole number of at least 1 (rhiza daemon set, rhiza daemon settings, rhiza.toml and the Rex daemon app's run-limit field), its type and description say so, and the daemon's resolved settings (daemonConf) carry whether it is auto

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/daemon-maxruns-auto: a new script with three accepted change sets, rhiza.daemon.maxRuns=auto and idle readings starts one run on the first --once poll and a second on the next (readings with room start a second run), and the saved state has max_runs_auto true; with maxRuns set to 1 a further poll starts none; (failure case) with RHIZA_TEST_LOAD1 and RHIZA_TEST_LOAD5 over rhiza.daemon.maxLoad, and again with the tmp-low hold on, an auto poll starts none; go test -trimpath ./internal/api/... and ./internal/daemon/... pass
fields.must_not: Read the host's load, memory or free space anew for the cap (use the poll's own pre-start readings); start more than one run per poll in auto; change a numeric maxRuns' behaviour; change rhiza run spawn's holds
fields.statement: With rhiza.daemon.maxRuns=auto the root daemon's poll sets the machine-wide cap it fills round-robin to the runs running plus one while every pre-start check has room, and to the runs running while any holds; the saved daemon state records max_runs_auto true beside max_runs, the cap that poll used; a number set for maxRuns pins the cap as before

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(daemon-status|health-runs-cap|describe-golden)': daemon-status gains a case whose saved state has max_runs_auto true and prints 'Max runs: auto (3 this poll)' and '"max_runs_auto": true'; health-runs-cap gains an auto case whose detail names the auto cap; describe-golden regenerated; (failure case) a state without max_runs_auto still prints 'Max runs: 3' and health still goes bad over a numeric cap
fields.must_not: Change the web UI or the Rex apps' display; drop or rename an existing --json field
fields.statement: rhiza daemon status says 'Max runs: auto (N this poll)' and its --json carries max_runs_auto when the last poll ran under auto, and rhiza health's daemon part writes 'runs: L live (auto cap N), S starting' and is never bad for being over the cap under auto
